newsitem.title: UK: Man Utd nets first half profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Man Utd nets first half profit rise.

text.p: Manchester United, England's top soccer club, produced another winning performance on Monday, reporting first half profit of 19.45 million pounds ($32 million).

Bigger crowds at the club's redeveloped Old Trafford stadium and higher television revenue helped the English champions to lift turnover by 68 percent to 50.1 million pounds in the six months to the end of January.

Chief executive Martin Edwards said the club's run to the semifinals of the European Champions' League had earned it around 7.5 million pounds. United play Germany's Borussia Dortmund in a semifinal first leg on Wednesday.

Interim dividend was raised to 1.9 pence per share from 1.6p a year ago. Shares in the club, which has a market capitalisation of over 400 million pounds, were unchanged at 641p by 1030 GMT on Monday.
Share analysts said the figures were very much in line with expectations.
"This is a good set of results. They delivered what we were looking for," said Nick Batram of stockbrokers Greig, Middleton. "This shows United to be clearly the biggest stock in the sector."

United, floated in 1991, have since enjoyed success on and off the field and have become the example to emulate for the growing number of British and European clubs either joining the stock market or planning a listing. They lead the English premier league as the season reaches its climax. Pre-tax profit of 19.45 million pounds was a 27 percent rise on last year's 15.28 million. This year's profit was boosted by transfer income of 3.8 million pounds, most of which came from the sale of former England international Lee Sharpe to Leeds United.

The club's gate receipts increased to 18.4 million pounds from 10.4 million following the completion of rebuilding at Old Trafford. Average home crowds topped 54,000 whereas they had been limited to 37,000 while the work was being done.
Television income rose to 5.9 million pounds from 3.3 million, thanks to a new deal between the premier league and BSkyB Plc plus extra money from rights to European matches.
The club's sponsorship income also topped five million pounds as the benefits of a new deal with kit manufacturer UMBRO came through.
Edwards said United would invest more than 3.5 million pounds on an enlarged club museum at Old Trafford. The existing site had 190,000 visitors last year and was proving too small.
The chief executive said that United, which has fans in Britain and Ireland, was considering opening new club shops in London, Dublin and Belfast.
